whoIsThisFor.heading: Who is the CPQ and Billing AP exam for?

personas.label: CPQ consultants expanding into Billing
personas.description: You already configure Salesforce CPQ and want to validate your ability to extend implementations through invoicing, payment processing, and revenue recognition.

personas.label: Finance and operations teams
personas.description: You manage invoice generation, subscription billing, and revenue schedules in Salesforce and need the credential to demonstrate your quote-to-cash expertise.

personas.label: Implementation partners
personas.description: You design end-to-end quote-to-cash solutions covering CPQ configuration through Billing deployment and want formal recognition of that full-lifecycle skill set.

examDifficulty.heading: Is the CPQ and Billing AP Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: The CPQ and Billing AP is moderately difficult. The ~65% passing score is standard, but the exam spans two products: Salesforce CPQ and Salesforce Billing, requiring knowledge of the full quote-to-cash lifecycle from product configuration through revenue recognition.
bullets: ~65% passing score: a standard threshold, but covering both CPQ and Billing doubles the surface area you need to study.
Two-product breadth: the exam tests CPQ configuration (bundles, rules, discounts) alongside Billing concepts (invoicing, usage billing, revenue recognition) in a single sitting.
Process knowledge critical: understanding the complete object chain from Quote through Invoice and Revenue Schedule is more important than memorizing individual features.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Walk through a complete quote-to-cash scenario in a developer org, creating a quote, generating an order, running an invoice, and configuring a revenue schedule, before booking the exam.

examFormat.heading: CPQ and Billing AP Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: The exam is proctored online or in-person. Here is the format:
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Expect scenario questions that follow a deal through the full lifecycle, from quote configuration to invoice generation and revenue recognition. Common patterns describe a billing requirement (monthly subscription billed in advance, usage-based overage) and ask which Billing configuration meets it.
bestWayToPass: Trace the full object chain: Know how Quote → Quote Line → Order → Order Product → Invoice → Invoice Line connects, and what triggers each object’s creation.
Study Billing rules deeply: Understand Bill Now vs. Bill in Advance vs. Bill in Arrears, billing frequency options, and how invoice consolidation groups charges by account.
Know usage-based billing: Understand how Usage Summaries aggregate consumption data, how Usage Rate Cards define pricing tiers, and how overage billing is calculated.

Review revenue recognition: Study how Revenue Schedules distribute revenue across accounting periods, the difference between ratable and event-based recognition, and how ASC 606 compliance is configured.

certificationCard.description: This exam covers the full Salesforce quote-to-cash process: CPQ product configuration, pricing rules, Billing invoice generation, subscription management, and revenue recognition.

keyConcepts.h2: CPQ Billing AP: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: Quote-to-Cash Process & Billing Setup
blocks.body: **CPQ** Billing extends Salesforce CPQ to handle the full Quote-to-Cash cycle: Quote → Order → Contract → Invoice → Payment. Billing must be enabled in CPQ Settings. The Order object bridges CPQ and Billing, when a Quote is contracted, an Order is created, and Billing creates invoices from Order Products. Billing Policies define the invoice generation schedule, payment terms, and invoice consolidation rules. Legal Entities represent the billing entities within a company, important for multi-national deployments. Tax Integration (Avalara, Vertex) calculates tax on invoices. The AP exam tests the configuration sequence for a new Billing setup and the object relationships in Quote-to-Cash.

blocks.heading: Invoice Generation & Billing Rules
blocks.body: Invoices are generated from Order Products based on Billing Rules, which define when and how charges are billed. Bill Now generates an invoice immediately. Bill in Advance bills at the start of a period. Bill in Arrears bills at the end of a period. Billing Frequency options: Monthly, Quarterly, Annually, or one-time. Invoice Run triggers invoice generation for all eligible Order Products. Invoice Lines represent individual charges. Credit Notes handle adjustments and cancellations. Billing Batches process large volumes asynchronously. The exam tests how to configure billing rules for common scenarios (annual subscription billed monthly, one-time setup fee billed immediately with first invoice).

blocks.heading: Usage-Based Billing
blocks.body: Usage Billing handles variable charges based on consumption: API calls, data transfer, seat count. Usage Summaries aggregate raw usage data into billable amounts for an invoice period. Usage Rate Cards define the price per unit or tier. Rated Usage is the calculated charge ready for invoicing. Usage data can be imported via CSV, API, or custom integration. Overage billing charges usage above the included amount in a subscription. The AP exam tests how to configure usage billing for a SaaS scenario (base subscription + overage), how usage summaries feed invoice lines, and how to test the billing calculation with sample usage data.

blocks.heading: Payment Processing & Dunning
blocks.body: Payment Gateways in **CPQ** Billing connect to payment processors (Stripe, CyberSource, Adyen) to tokenize and charge payment methods. Payment Terms define when payment is due after invoice generation (Net 30, Due on Receipt). Auto-Pay automatically charges the stored payment method on the invoice due date. Dunning Processes handle failed payments, automated retry schedules, dunning emails, and account holds after N failed attempts. Payment Allocations apply payments to specific invoices. Refunds and Credit Memos reverse billed charges. The exam tests how to configure auto-pay, design a dunning workflow, and handle the scenario where a payment fails and needs to be retried.

blocks.heading: Revenue Recognition & Reporting
blocks.body: Revenue Recognition in **CPQ** Billing aligns with ASC 606 and IFRS 15 standards. Revenue Schedules distribute invoice revenue across the service period rather than recognizing it all at invoice date. Revenue Recognition Rules define when revenue is recognized (ratably over subscription term, point-in-time for one-time charges). Revenue Distribution Transactions record the recognized amounts per period. Finance Period controls define accounting period boundaries. Revenue Reporting surfaces recognized vs. deferred revenue. The exam tests how to configure revenue recognition for a subscription scenario, how to handle amendments that modify in-period revenue schedules, and key reporting objects.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Salesforce CPQ and Billing Accredited Professional Exam
scenarioTips.intro: The CPQ & Billing AP exam tests the full quote-to-cash process. Focus on CPQ configuration, Billing order generation, invoice processing, and revenue recognition, the complete lifecycle from quoting to recognizing revenue.

blocks.heading: CPQ-to-Billing Object Chain
blocks.body: Master the object chain: Quote → Quote Line → Order → Order Product → Asset/Subscription → Contract → Invoice Line → Invoice. Know what triggers each object's creation and the key fields at each step.

blocks.heading: Billing Order Generation
blocks.body: Know how to configure Order generation: Order Start Date, billing frequency, and how Billing handles co-termination for amendments. Understand how Net New vs. Upgrade vs. Downgrade orders generate different billing actions.

blocks.heading: Invoice Processing
blocks.body: Know the Invoice Run process: how to configure run schedules, what constitutes an invoice (grouping by account, billing day), and how the Legal Entity and Invoice Status workflow controls invoice approval.

blocks.heading: Subscription Management
blocks.body: Know how to handle subscription changes mid-term: Cancel (immediate/end-of-term), Reduce Quantity, Add Products, and how proration is calculated for each type of change.

blocks.heading: Revenue Recognition
blocks.body: Know how Revenue Schedules distribute revenue across periods, how the Accounting Period configuration controls recognition timing, and how to handle ramp deals with non-linear revenue schedules.

sampleQuestions.question: A contract is signed and the customer should now be invoiced monthly. What does CPQ Billing create to make this happen?
options: A separate opportunity for each monthly invoice that needs to be raised
A billing schedule from the order product
A renewal contract covering each of the monthly periods in the term
A fresh quote that is generated automatically at the start of every month
sampleQuestions.explanation: Billing schedules hold the periods and amounts to be invoiced, and they are created from the order products once the order is activated.
whyWrong: Opportunities track sales, not the invoicing of an existing contract.
Renewals cover the next term rather than this term's invoices.
Quotes come before the order; they are not produced per invoice.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the difference between an invoice and an invoice line in CPQ Billing?
options: The invoice is for subscriptions and the invoice line is for one-off products
The invoice holds the tax while each invoice line holds the payment received
The invoice is the document; the lines are the charges on it
The invoice is a draft while the invoice line is the posted and final version
sampleQuestions.explanation: An invoice groups invoice lines, and each line carries a charge for a product over a period.
whyWrong: Both subscription and one-off charges appear as invoice lines.
Tax and payments are tracked separately from this distinction.
Draft and posted are statuses on the invoice, not the difference between the two objects.

sampleQuestions.question: A customer upgrades mid-term and should only pay for the remaining months. What handles this?
options: Proration on the amendment
A new contract that replaces the original one from the beginning of the term
A manual adjustment entered by finance on the next invoice to be raised
A credit note issued for the full value of the original annual contract
sampleQuestions.explanation: An amendment prorates the change across the time left in the term, so the customer is charged for the period they actually get.
whyWrong: Replacing the contract loses the original term and its history.
Manual adjustment is error-prone when the platform calculates it.
A full credit note reverses more than the change requires.

sampleQuestions.question: What does revenue recognition in CPQ Billing determine?
options: How much discount a sales user is allowed to apply to a given quote line
Which of the available payment methods the customer is permitted to use
When revenue is recorded, as opposed to when it is invoiced
Which currency the invoice will be presented in for an overseas customer
sampleQuestions.explanation: Invoicing and revenue recognition are separate: you can invoice a year up front and recognise the revenue month by month.
whyWrong: Discount limits are set in CPQ pricing and approvals.
Payment methods are part of payment handling, not revenue recognition.
Currency is a separate field on the account and the order.

sampleQuestions.question: An invoice has been posted and contains an error. What is the correct way to fix it?
options: Edit the posted invoice directly and then save the corrected version of it
Issue a credit note against it
Leave it and note the correction in the description field on the account
Delete the invoice from the system and create a replacement for the customer
sampleQuestions.explanation: Posted invoices are financial records, so corrections are made by issuing a credit note rather than altering history.
whyWrong: Posted invoices are locked precisely so they cannot be edited.
A note on the account does not correct the customer's balance.
Deleting a financial record destroys the audit trail.

sampleQuestions.question: What triggers the creation of an order in a CPQ and Billing flow?
options: Saving the quote for the first time in the Quote Line Editor as a draft
Ordering the quote once it is accepted
Adding the first subscription product to the quote during configuration
Submitting the quote into the approval process for a manager to review
sampleQuestions.explanation: The order is created from the accepted quote, and it is the order products that drive billing.
whyWrong: Saving a draft quote does not commit anything.
Adding products changes the quote, not the order.
Approval is a step before acceptance, not order creation.

sampleQuestions.question: A customer pays less than the invoiced amount. How should this be recorded?
options: As an amendment to the contract reducing the total value of the term
As a brand new invoice raised for the balance that is still outstanding
As a partial payment allocated against the invoice
As a credit note for the difference between the two amounts involved
sampleQuestions.explanation: Payments are allocated to invoices, and a partial payment leaves the remainder outstanding.
whyWrong: The contract value has not changed because the customer underpaid.
The original invoice still carries the balance; a second one would double it.
A credit note reduces what is owed, which is not what a short payment means.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the purpose of a billing rule in CPQ Billing?
options: It restricts which products a particular sales user is allowed to add to a quote
It decides which approval chain a heavily discounted quote must travel through
It determines the order in which quote lines appear in the Quote Line Editor
It controls how and when charges are invoiced
sampleQuestions.explanation: Billing rules govern invoicing behaviour, such as timing and whether a charge is billed at all.
whyWrong: Product availability is controlled by product rules and price books.
Approval routing is handled by CPQ approvals.
Line display order is a presentation setting on the quote.

sampleQuestions.question: A subscription runs from January to December and is invoiced quarterly. How many billing periods result?
options: Twelve, because a subscription is always invoiced on a monthly basis
One, because the whole subscription term is invoiced as a single charge
Four
Three, because the first quarter is billed as part of the order itself
sampleQuestions.explanation: Quarterly invoicing over a twelve-month term produces four periods, each covering three months.
whyWrong: Monthly invoicing would produce twelve, but the frequency here is quarterly.
A single charge would be annual invoicing, not quarterly.
No quarter is absorbed into the order; all four are billed.

sampleQuestions.question: What does a tax rule in CPQ Billing do?
options: It decides how tax is calculated on a charge
It prevents an invoice from being posted until a tax reference is supplied
It reports the total tax collected across the year for a given legal entity
It converts the tax amount into the functional currency of the organisation
sampleQuestions.explanation: Tax rules and treatments determine the rate and method applied to a charge, whether calculated internally or by an external engine.
whyWrong: Posting controls come from billing rules and validation, not tax rules.
Reporting is a separate activity from the rule that calculates tax.
Currency conversion is handled by the currency configuration.

sampleQuestions.question: Why would an implementation use evergreen rather than fixed-term subscriptions?
options: The products involved are one-off purchases with no recurring element
The service continues until somebody cancels it
The contract has to be renegotiated at the end of each and every term
The customer wants to be invoiced once annually rather than every month
sampleQuestions.explanation: Evergreen subscriptions have no end date and continue billing until cancelled, which suits services with no natural term.
whyWrong: One-off products are not subscriptions at all.
Renegotiation at term end describes a fixed-term arrangement.
Invoice frequency is set separately from whether the term is fixed.

sampleQuestions.question: An order is activated but no invoice appears. What is a likely cause?
options: The billing schedule has not yet reached its next billing date
The quote was never submitted to a manager for approval before ordering
The customer record is missing the industry field required for reporting
The product was configured as a bundle rather than a standalone product
sampleQuestions.explanation: Invoices are generated when the invoice run picks up schedules whose billing date has arrived, so a future date means nothing to invoice yet.
whyWrong: Approval affects the quote, not whether invoicing runs.
Reporting fields do not block invoice generation.
Bundles bill normally through their order products.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the role of an invoice run?
options: It recalculates the prices on all open quotes against the current price book
It closes the accounting period so that no further postings can be made
It sends a copy of every outstanding invoice to the customer by email again
It generates invoices from schedules that are due
sampleQuestions.explanation: The invoice run is the scheduled or manual process that picks up due billing schedules and produces invoices.
whyWrong: Quote pricing is recalculated in CPQ, not by the invoice run.
Period close is an accounting activity outside the invoice run.
Delivery of invoices is a separate step from generating them.

sampleQuestions.question: A customer cancels a subscription halfway through a prepaid annual term. What is normally produced?
options: A renewal quote starting from the date the cancellation was processed
An amendment increasing the contract value for the cancelled period
A new invoice covering the remaining months that were never delivered
A credit for the unused portion of the term
sampleQuestions.explanation: Cancelling a prepaid term leaves the customer in credit for the service they will not receive.
whyWrong: A renewal is for continuing service, not for a cancellation.
Cancellation reduces rather than increases the contract value.
Invoicing undelivered service would charge them twice.

sampleQuestions.question: Which best describes the relationship between CPQ and Billing?
options: CPQ produces the order; Billing invoices what was ordered
Billing produces the quote and CPQ then collects the payment from the customer
They are alternative products and an organisation chooses one or the other
CPQ handles subscriptions while Billing handles only one-off product charges
sampleQuestions.explanation: CPQ covers configure, price and quote through to the order. Billing takes the order and turns it into invoices, payments and revenue.
whyWrong: Quoting is CPQ's role, and payment collection belongs to Billing.
They are designed to work together across quote to cash.
Billing invoices both subscription and one-off charges.
